messages.author: b4d6c0475b0419ac
messages.subject: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis
parts:
After multiple attempts, finally I can run a group syntax. But there is something curious in output.

If syntax is: fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero") the output shows all results without constraints.

If syntax is: fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero", estimator = "MLR", mimic = "Mplus") the output shows constraints in loadings and intercepts. 

I looking for a solution with Robust Fit indices. 

Cordially

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis
parts: Look at the documentation for multiple-group CFA in Mplus, starting with example 5.14 (available at the Mplus home page). Measurement invariance is the default. So this is exactly what you should expect.

messages.subject: Re: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis
parts:
Patrick:

Thanks a lot. You are right it was "Mplus". Now I have other question related to invariance. My output shows factor loadings, regressions, covariance, intercepts and variance.
For configurational invariance is:  fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero", estimator = "MLR")
For metric invariance is:  fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero", group.equal = c ("loadings"), estimator = "MLR")
For scalar invariance is  fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero",   group.equal = c ("loadings" ,"intercepts"), estimator = "MLR"
For scalar invariance is  fit <- sem(semmodel, data = Estudios_de_Aceptacion_UPR_2020,  group = "Genero",   group.equal = c ("loadings" ,"intercepts", "variance"), estimator = "MLR"  

I don't see residuals in the output. My question is can I include variance or covariance?

Look at the documentation for multiple-group CFA in Mplus, starting with example 5.14 (available at the Mplus home page). Measurement invariance is the default. So this is exactly what you should expect.

I looking for a solution with Robust Fit indices. 

Cordially

messages.subject: Re: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis
parts:
You're working with ordered data, aren't you? So you don't have intercepts and residual variances. Just loadings and thresholds (should be constrained simultaneously, not stepwise).

Also, (factor) variances aren't part of measurement invariance testing.

messages.subject: Re: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis
parts:
Great! 

But, for the invariance test, what constraints do I need to include?  My output only has Latent Variables (loadings), Regressions, Covariances, Intercepts and Variance. 
I was considering:
 loadings for metric invariance, 
loadings and intercepts for scalar
loadings, regressions, covariance and intercepts  for strict. 

I saw this information in https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html but I 'm not sure if lv.variances and lv. covariances are options for my analysis. 






Patrick, thanks for your advice.
From: lav...@googlegroups.com <lav...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Patrick (Malone Quantitative) <mal...@malonequantitative.com>
Sent: Monday, November 2, 2020 9:22 PM

To: lav...@googlegroups.com <lav...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: MLR estimation in Multigroup Analysis

Yes.

lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
>
> Hello Patrick:
>
> I run the CFA and SEM model with MLR estimation treating variables as continuous.  This estimation works well with my data. Now, I try multigroup analysis and invariance test with gender and age.  Now I 'm confused because,  I think I have to use the same estimation with group analysis. Is this correct?
>
>
>

>> Ana,
>>

>> >
